scope: Week 4a: framework provisions for seven framework families (the five existing families plus Meta and Microsoft), recorded absences, provision-level changes, the first contested records, and the three week-3 stop cases (recorded separately in review/week4a-stop-case-decisions-2026-10-03.json). Schema 2.8. All new records are seeds with machine-checked evidence; no editorial state changed.

proposingPass.agents: Four fresh-context extraction subagents (Claude Opus 5.5, claude-opus-5-5), one per family group, proposing provisions, absences and changes from local UTF-8 text of each cited edition; the curator (the Claude Code session, same model) verified every quote mechanically, applied curated decisions and ingested.
proposingPass.method: Quote verification removes invisible format characters and collapses whitespace; words, punctuation, quote marks and dashes must match. Quotes found only after ignoring spaces were accepted for four RSP sentences whose text layers drop word spaces, each noted in its evidence. The quotation policy (at most about five quotes and 250 words per document) bounded provisions per edition.

qa.design: Two fresh-context readers checked every provision-change claim independently and blind to each other; a third fresh-context agent adjudicated the disputed claims and two flagged by one reader. Both readers also checked targeted risky records (contested records, stop-case decisions, new family records) and each checked a different seeded random sample of other new records.
qa.independence: All agents were subagents of the proposing session using the same model family on the same machine; execution independence is not established. Readers received records and sources but not the proposer’s verification notes on what matched, nor each other’s results.

selection.method: mulberry32 PRNG, draws without replacement from ID-sorted pools; provisions exclude the contested provision (targeted)

As written, v3.3 appears to have no severity qualifier. Also 'end-to-end development' paraphrases 'end-to-end agent design and deployment'.

Incomplete. v3.0 also adds, in its Note on Machine Learning R&D CCLs, that 'our alert threshold may be defined based on these sources of information [own ML R&D progress], rather than on evaluation scores'. v2.0 has no such allowance (searched). The record's own v3.1-vs-v3.0 change treats this note as part of v3.0's provision, so its introduction in v3.0 should be stated here.

Misattribution: the GovAI post (by Sophie Williams and Jonas Freund) says 'GovAI research blog posts represent the views of their authors rather than the views of the organization', so 'GovAI's stated concern/concludes' is wrong. results.reasoning: Read v3.3 PDF p. 7, row ‘Novel chemical/biological weapons production’, left column with fns 4–7; v3.2 PDF p. 7, same row (no footnotes in that cell); and the v3.3 change log at PDF p. 20 (printed p. 19), item (1), which says the update ‘revises our threshold for novel chemical/biological weapons production to better track the threat model of concern’. Both compared-provision quotes are exact and the changelog basis is right. The record correctly identifies the reframing (functional substitution for scarce expertise in v3.3; significant help to threat actors in v3.2), so it is not incorrect. I agree with both readers that the statement describes v3.3 asymmetrically. It gives v3.2's severity bar (‘far beyond those of past catastrophes such as COVID-19’) but drops v3.3's own: ‘with potential for catastrophic harm’, with fn 4 ‘In particular, weapons with the potential to cause events with consequences comparable to or worse than those of COVID-19’. As stored, v3.3 appears to have no severity qualifier and no COVID-19 reference. It also renders ‘end-to-end agent design and deployment (including, as relevant, agent design, verification and validation, formulation, and dissemination)’ as ‘end-to-end development’. Set against v3.2's ‘create/obtain and deploy’, this suggests a narrowing to development that the text does not make. Minor: ‘currently’ is dropped, and ‘operationalized as’ replaces the source's ‘That is’. Fn 4 qualifies the very element the statement contrasts, so it belongs in the statement. Fns 5–7 are illustrative (‘For example’, ‘E.g.’) and can stay in the evidence. Companion edit: update the ‘later’ evidence paraphrase to match the v3.3 half of the replacement. Its locator already covers fns 4–7. Basis and derivation need no change.

edit.replacement: v3.3's threshold covers AI systems that can functionally substitute for the scarce human expertise that is currently the primary barrier to novel development of chemical and biological weapons with potential for catastrophic harm (footnote: “In particular, weapons with the potential to cause events with consequences comparable to or worse than those of COVID-19”); that is, a well-resourced team could, using the model, accomplish the end-to-end agent design and deployment (including, as relevant, agent design, verification and validation, formulation, and dissemination) that would otherwise require recruiting one of a small number of world-leading specialists. v3.2's threshold covered AI systems with the ability to significantly help threat actors (for example, moderately resourced expert-backed teams) create/obtain and deploy chemical and/or biological weapons with potential for catastrophic damages far beyond those of past catastrophes such as COVID-19.

results.reasoning: Read v3.0 PDF p. 5, §1.3 ‘Analysis’ bullet, and the Note on Machine Learning R&D CCLs (PDF pp. 5–6); and v2.0 PDF p. 3 in both copies. Both quotes are exact and the stored contrast (‘before the evaluations are run again’ to ‘before a risk assessment is conducted again’) is accurate. The neighbouring sentence on running early warning evaluations more frequently or adjusting the alert threshold is identical in both editions, so it is not a difference. The readers are right that the record is incomplete. v3.0's Note ends ‘Similarly, our alert threshold may be defined based on these sources of information, rather than on evaluation scores’. ‘These sources’ are information about Google DeepMind's own progress at accelerating ML R&D. Full-text searches of both v2.0 text copies found no counterpart: no ‘evaluation scores’, ‘sources of information’ or ‘own progress’. v2.0 lists ML R&D among its misuse domains with no such note. The dataset's v3.1-vs-v3.0 change record, as reproduced in the reader packet, treats this note as part of v3.0's alert-threshold provision. Without this edit, the version chain shows the note in v3.0 but never records its introduction. Companion edits are needed for the new clause to be evidenced. Extend the ‘later’ evidence locator to ‘PDF pp. 5–6, §1.3 Outline of Our Risk Assessment Process, “Analysis” bullet, second sentence; Note on Machine Learning R&D CCLs, last sentence’ and update its paraphrase. Add the Note and the v2.0 full-text check to the inferenceRationale premises. Derivation (inferred) and basis (document_comparison) stay as they are.

edit.replacement: v3.0’s alert thresholds for its early warning evaluations are designed to flag when a CCL may be reached before a risk assessment is conducted again, and its Note on Machine Learning R&D CCLs adds that the alert threshold may be defined based on sources of information about Google DeepMind’s own progress at accelerating ML R&D, rather than on evaluation scores; v2.0’s alert threshold flagged when a CCL may be reached before the evaluations are run again, and v2.0 contains no such note.

results.reasoning: Read AASF v2 PDF pp. 15–17: Table 1 and §3.3; the cited sentence is exact at p. 17. Read FAF v1.1 PDF p. 12, §3.3; the sentence is exact, also appears in the executive summary at p. 4, and is identical in the 2025-02-13 and 2025-03-28 expressions. Also read FAF Table 1 (p. 13) and the v2 change log at PDF p. 44 (‘Critical threshold changed from “Stop” to “Develop with Mitigations.”’). The statement is accurate to both operative sentences and to the changelog. Reader A's point is real. Table 1's critical measures are: pause development while investigating whether barriers remain; mitigate to moderate levels ‘to the extent possible’; run threat modelling, with possible reassignment to another threshold; and otherwise ‘do not further develop the model until such a time as adequate mitigations have been identified’. So v1.1's stop was conditional. But the statement keeps both of v1.1's own qualifiers: ‘cannot be mitigated’ and the cross-reference to the Table 1 measures. It does not call the stop unconditional or permanent. The Table 1 process elaborates the statement rather than contradicting it, and the contrast drawn is the one the changelog itself draws. v1.1's resumption condition (‘adequate mitigations have been identified’) also differs in wording from v2's (‘risk assessments are complete and safeguards are defined, implemented and validated to reduce risk to the moderate or lower risk threshold’), so the contrast is a genuine textual one. The high-threshold record differs: there the v1.1 measure is not referenced at all. No edit required. Non-blocking: ‘reaches the critical threshold’ compresses v1.1's ‘is assessed to have reached the critical risk threshold’. If the editor wants parallel treatment with the high-threshold record, a faithful optional addition to the v1.1 half is ‘…, Table 1 listing a pause in development, mitigation to moderate levels to the extent possible, and no further development until adequate mitigations have been identified’.

Read the AASF v2 Table 1 High row (PDF p. 15; quote exact) and FAF v1.1 §4.2 (PDF p. 17). The FAF quote is exact in the 2025-02-13 expression only; the 2025-03-28 expression reads ‘threat scenario’ for ‘catastrophic outcome’, as the compared provision already records. Also read the FAF Table 1 High row (PDF p. 13, checked in both expressions) and the change log at PDF p. 44 (‘High threshold measure changed from “Do not release” to “Deploy with mitigations.”’). The contrast is accurate and matches the changelog, so it is not incorrect. Both readers noted, and I confirm, that v1.1's Table 1 High row pairs the ‘Do not release’ label with the Measures-column entry ‘Implement mitigations to reduce risk to moderate levels.’ The stored statement uses mitigation to moderate as the v2 side of the contrast and omits v1.1's own measure in the same table the record cites. A reader would therefore take the mitigation element to be new in v2. That is a material omission for a change record keyed to this measure. Unlike the critical-measure record, this statement does not even point to the Table 1 measure. The replacement adds it without interpreting whether v1.1 permitted release once risk was reduced; the text does not say. Companion edit: extend the ‘earlier’ evidence locator's parenthesis to ‘Table 1, PDF p. 13, High row: label “Do not release”; Measures column “Implement mitigations to reduce risk to moderate levels”’ and update its paraphrase. Table 1 is identical in both v1.1 expressions, so no new expression qualification is needed.

edit.replacement: v2's high-threshold measure (“Deploy with mitigations”) is to proceed with deployment of the Frontier AI only if sufficient mitigations are defined, implemented and validated to reduce risk to that of a moderate or lower model, whereas v1.1 states that a frontier AI at the high risk threshold will not be released externally, and its Table 1 pairs the high threshold's “Do not release” label with the measure “Implement mitigations to reduce risk to moderate levels.”
